claims.text: The starting material is an as-fabricated nanoscale HEA multilayer with alternating FCC/BCC or compositionally distinct layers, coherent or semi-coherent interfaces, and minimal prior plastic deformation.
The proposed mechanism requires layer thicknesses on the order of 10 nm or less.
Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is controlled by dislocation accumulation at interfaces between FCC and BCC or compositionally distinct layers.
Nanoscale multilayer interfaces impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocations form pile-ups and local stress concentrations at the interfaces.
Interface dislocation accumulation and its local stresses alter short-range order in adjacent layers.
High local stresses near interfaces produce subtle changes in lattice parameters.
Stress-induced lattice or short-range-order changes activate secondary slip systems.
The local stress and ordering changes can activate deformation twinning.
Cooperative dislocation activity and secondary deformation mechanisms progressively accommodate plastic strain.
This cooperative deformation preserves the multilayer's overall structural integrity during progressive strain.
Plastic strain increasingly localizes near layer interfaces as loading time increases.
Sustained loading increases dislocation density near multilayer interfaces.
Deformation twins should occasionally appear during sustained loading.
Local ordering transitions should become detectable near the interfaces.
The coating should initially exhibit gradual strain hardening.
The initial hardening should be followed by softening once interface damage becomes critical.
At excessively high temperatures, deformation may switch from interface-controlled accumulation to more uniform plastic flow or premature failure.
Excessively wide layers or degraded interfaces may suppress interface-controlled accumulation and produce uniform flow or premature failure.
The relative contributions of dynamic short-range ordering and dislocation pile-up may vary with chemistry or layer thickness.
